title: No Perfect Mondrian Partition Has a Common Tile Area Supported on Two Primes
abstract: The Mondrian art problem asks for the minimum defect, the difference between the largest and smallest tile areas, over partitions of an $n \times n$ square into at least two pairwise noncongruent integer-sided rectangles. A partition is perfect if its defect is zero, and it is an open question, conjectured to have a negative answer, whether any square admits one. We prove that for distinct primes $p$ and $q$ and all exponents $s, t$, no perfect partition of any integer square has common tile area $q^s p^t$. Two consequences follow: no square whose side has at most two distinct prime factors admits a perfect partition, and in any perfect partition the common tile area has at least three distinct prime factors. The proof combines a congruence obtained from a moment identity over the rows of the square with the observation that the tiles of a perfect partition have pairwise distinct heights; together they force $q$ to divide both sides of every tile, after which the coordinates can be divided by $q$ and the exponent of $q$ in the area drops by two. Every result here is formalized and checked in Lean 4.
introduction:
The Mondrian art problem concerns partitions of an $n \times n$ square into axis-aligned rectangles with positive integer side lengths. To exclude trivial configurations such as identical parallel strips, the rectangles of an admissible partition are required to be pairwise noncongruent: no two share the same unordered pair of side lengths. The defect of a partition $P$ is
$$\text{def}(P) = \max_{R \in P} |R| - \min_{R \in P} |R|,$$
and the Mondrian number $M(n)$ is the least defect over all admissible partitions of the $n \times n$ square into two or more rectangles.

A partition of defect zero is called perfect: its rectangles are pairwise noncongruent and yet all have the same area $A$, so that $kA = n^2$ when there are $k$ of them. As arXiv:2610.19193 recalls in Section 1, it is still an open problem whether $M(n) = 0$ for some $n$, though it is conjectured that no such $n$ exists. That paper also notes that a single perfect partition would give infinitely many, since scaling all sides by a common factor preserves the defect zero, and that perfect partitions have been excluded computationally for every $n \le 1000$ (arXiv:2311.02385). On the theoretical side, the prime-power case is classical: squares whose side is a prime power admit no perfect partition (arXiv:2007.09639, Theorem 4.1, by counting the available shapes), and density results show that a positive proportion of integers $n$ have $M(n) > 0$.

This post gives an obstruction that holds for every square at once and is phrased in terms of the common tile area rather than the side. The main theorem, `mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_area`, states that for distinct primes $p$ and $q$ and arbitrary exponents $s$ and $t$, no perfect admissible partition of any integer square has all its tiles of area $q^s p^t$. It extends `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area`, the same statement for a prime-power area $p^t$. Two corollaries are formalized:

- `mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_powers`: for distinct primes $p, q$ and all exponents $e, f$, the square of side $q^f p^e$ admits no perfect partition. Together with the prime-power case, this excludes every side length with at most two distinct prime factors, with no restriction on the exponents.
- `mondrian_perfect_area_three_prime_factors`: in any perfect partition of any square, the common tile area has at least three distinct prime factors.

An earlier, weaker result in the same development, `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_mul_prime_pow`, treated the sides $q p^e$ by a different route, counting the factor pairs of the area that fit in the square; it is the case $f = 1$ of the first corollary. The key new ingredient is a divisibility lemma: if the common area is $q^s p^t$ and $q$ divides $n$, then $q$ divides both side lengths of every tile. Its proof uses only a linear identity over the rows of the square, the distinctness of tile heights in a perfect partition, and the fact that the tile heights not divisible by $q$ form a chain under divisibility.
result:
Theorem (`mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_area`). Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct primes and let $s, t, n \in \mathbb{N}$. There is no list $P$ of rectangles such that `mondrian_is_partition n P`, `mondrian_defect P = 0`, and every $r \in P$ has area $q^s p^t$.

The statement places no condition on $n$: it is an obstruction on the common tile area alone. The case $s = 0$ is `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area`, which excludes a prime-power common area $p^t$ (including area 1).

Corollary 1 (`mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_powers`). Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct primes and $e, f \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $\neg \exists P,\ \text{mondrian\_is\_partition}(q^f p^e, P) \wedge \text{mondrian\_defect}(P) = 0$.

Indeed, by `mondrian_perfect_area_product` the common area of a perfect partition divides $n^2 = q^{2f} p^{2e}$, so it has the form $q^s p^t$. Every integer $n \ge 2$ with at most two distinct prime factors has the form $q^f p^e$, so no such square has a perfect partition.

Corollary 2 (`mondrian_perfect_area_three_prime_factors`). If `mondrian_is_partition n P`, `mondrian_defect P = 0` and $r \in P$, then the area of $r$ has at least three distinct prime factors.

Any hypothetical perfect partition must therefore have a tile area divisible by three distinct primes, and since the area divides $n^2$, its side $n$ must have at least three distinct prime factors as well. The smallest side lengths left open by these results are $30, 42, 60, 66, \dots$; all sides up to 1000 are excluded by the computation of arXiv:2311.02385, so the results here add the infinite family of two-prime sides and a structural restriction on the area of any counterexample.
proof:
Throughout, $P$ is a perfect admissible partition of the $n \times n$ square; we write $w(r)$ and $h(r)$ for the width and height of $r \in P$, and $r = (x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1)$ for its coordinates.

Step 1 (distinct heights). Two distinct tiles of $P$ have distinct heights. If $h(r) = h(r')$, then since $w(r)h(r) = w(r')h(r')$ and heights are positive, also $w(r) = w(r')$, so $r$ and $r'$ are congruent, which admissibility forbids.

Step 2 (a moment identity over the rows). For every integer-valued function $f$ on the row levels $0, 1, \dots, n$,
$$\sum_{r \in P} w(r)\,\bigl(f(y_1(r)) - f(y_0(r))\bigr) = n\,\bigl(f(n) - f(0)\bigr).$$
Writing $f(y_1) - f(y_0)$ as a telescoping sum over the rows $y_0 \le y < y_1$, the left side becomes $\sum_{y < n} (f(y+1) - f(y)) \sum_{r \ni y} w(r)$, and the widths of the tiles crossing any row $y$ add up to $n$ because the tiles partition that row of cells.

Step 3 (an isolated tile). Let $d \mid n$ and $m \ge 1$. Suppose $r \in P$ has $m \nmid h(r)$, and every other tile $r'$ has $d \mid w(r')$ or $m \mid h(r')$. Then $d \mid w(r)$. To see this, apply Step 2 to $f(y) = 1$ if $y \equiv y_1(r) \pmod m$ and $f(y) = 0$ otherwise. The right side is a multiple of $n$, hence of $d$. A tile $r'$ with $m \mid h(r')$ has $y_0(r') \equiv y_1(r') \pmod m$, so its increment of $f$ is 0; a tile with $d \mid w(r')$ contributes a multiple of $d$. For $r$ itself, $y_0(r) \not\equiv y_1(r) \pmod m$ because $m \nmid h(r)$, so its increment is exactly 1 and its term is $w(r)$. Reducing the identity modulo $d$ gives $d \mid w(r)$.

Step 4 (prime chains). Let $d \mid n$, let $p$ be prime and $C > 0$, and suppose every tile whose width is not divisible by $d$ has height of the form $C p^a$. Then every width is divisible by $d$. Otherwise, among the tiles with $d \nmid w$, choose $z$ of least height $C p^a$ and put $m = C p^{a+1}$. Then $m \nmid h(z)$ since $0 < h(z) < m$. Every other tile $r'$ with $d \nmid w(r')$ has height $C p^b$ with $C p^b \ne C p^a$ by Step 1 and $C p^b \ge C p^a$ by minimality, so $b \ge a + 1$ and $m \mid h(r')$. Step 3 now gives $d \mid w(z)$, a contradiction.

Step 5 (both sides divisible by $q$). Suppose every tile has area $q^s p^t$ and $q \mid n$. If $q \nmid w(r)$, then from $w(r)h(r) = q^s p^t$ the full power $q^s$ divides $h(r)$, and the remaining factor is a divisor of $p^t$, so $h(r) = q^s p^a$ for some $a$. Step 4 with $d = q$ and $C = q^s$ shows that $q$ divides every width. Applying the same argument to the partition reflected in the diagonal, which is again perfect and admissible, shows that $q$ divides every height.

Step 6 (descent). If $q$ divides $n$ and both sides of every tile, and the common area is $q^2 B$, then dividing all coordinates by $q$ gives a perfect admissible partition of the $(n/q)$-square with common area $B$. Disjointness, coverage and noncongruence all transfer, because a cell $(i, j)$ of the divided rectangle corresponds to the cell $(q(i+1) - 1, q(j+1) - 1)$ of the original one. The same coordinate division underlies `mondrian_perfect_partition_div`.

Proof of the theorem. We use strong induction on $s$, for all $n$ and $P$ at once. If $s = 0$, the area is $p^t$ and `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area` applies. That result is proved by the same scheme with the single prime $p$: Step 5, applied to the area $p^t$ (a second prime with exponent zero), makes $p$ divide both sides of every tile, descent lowers the exponent by two, and area 1 is impossible because two $1 \times 1$ tiles are congruent. If $s \ge 1$, pick $z \in P$. By `mondrian_perfect_area_product`, $|P| \cdot q^s p^t = n^2$, so $q \mid n^2$ and hence $q \mid n$. By Step 5, $q$ divides both sides of $z$, so $q^2 \mid q^s p^t$; as $q^2$ is coprime to $p^t$, this gives $s \ge 2$. Writing $q^s p^t = q^2 \cdot q^{s-2} p^t$, Step 6 yields a perfect admissible partition of the $(n/q)$-square with common area $q^{s-2} p^t$, which the induction hypothesis for $s - 2 < s$ excludes.

Proof of Corollary 1. The case $f = 0$ is the prime-power side, `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power`. For $f \ge 1$, the common area $A$ divides $q^{2f} p^{2e}$ by `mondrian_perfect_area_product`, so $A = q^s p^t$, and the same divisibility and descent steps reduce the side from $q^{f} p^e$ to $q^{f-1} p^e$, closing an induction on $f$.

Proof of Corollary 2. Suppose the common area $A$ has at most two distinct prime factors. It is positive, so it is 1, a prime power $p^t$, or $q^s p^t$ with $p \ne q$. Area 1 is impossible since all tiles would be congruent unit squares; the other two cases are `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area` and `mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_area`.
discussion:
The theorem shows that the common tile area of a perfect Mondrian partition cannot be supported on two primes, whatever the size of the square. Its corollaries exclude every side length with at most two distinct prime factors and show that a counterexample to the zero-defect conjecture needs a tile area, and hence a side, divisible by at least three distinct primes.

The argument rests on a linear identity over the rows of the square and on the distinctness of tile heights. Step 3 isolates one tile with the indicator of a residue class of rows; Step 4 makes this possible whenever the heights of the tiles with width prime to $d$ form a chain $C p^a$, because the smallest of them is then the only one whose height fails to be divisible by the next element of the chain. With two primes, the cofactor of a width prime to $q$ is forced into such a chain. With a third prime $\ell$ in the area, a width prime to $q$ leaves the height $q^s p^a \ell^b$, and these numbers are no longer totally ordered by divisibility, so the isolation step does not apply directly.

The central question recalled in Section 1 of arXiv:2610.19193, whether $M(n) = 0$ for some $n \ge 3$, remains open. The smallest sides not covered by these results, such as $30 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$, are excluded only by the computation for $n \le 1000$ in arXiv:2311.02385, and no uniform argument is known for sides with three or more distinct prime factors.

references.title: A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem

research: Excludes every square side q*p^e for distinct primes p,q with no bound on e and no ordering restriction on the primes; arXiv:2007.09639 Theorem 4.1 excludes prime powers and products of at most three primes but does not give this exponent-uniform two-prime family

Excludes perfect partitions of every integer square when the common tile area is q^s*p^t for distinct primes p,q and arbitrary exponents, and hence excludes all square sides supported on two primes. The prime-power and small prime-product exclusions of arXiv:2007.09639 Theorem 4.1 and the density theorem in HAL:hal-05729522v2 do not give this uniform common-area restriction
tier_why: A uniform obstruction for every square: no perfect partition has a common tile area supported on two primes, so every side with at most two distinct prime factors is excluded and any counterexample's tile area needs three primes; the zero-defect question itself stays open.

zh.title: 不存在公共块面积由两个素数支撑的完美蒙德里安划分
zh.abstract: 蒙德里安艺术问题询问将一个 $n \times n$ 正方形划分为至少两个两两不全等的整边长矩形的划分中，最大与最小块面积之差（即缺陷）的最小值。若一个划分的缺陷为零，则称其为完美划分；是否存在正方形允许完美划分是一个未决问题，且被猜想为否定答案。我们证明了对于不同素数 $p$ 和 $q$ 以及任意指数 $s, t$，任何整数正方形的完美划分其公共块面积均不可能为 $q^s p^t$。由此可得两个推论：边长至多含有两个不同素因子的正方形均不存在完美划分，且在任何完美划分中，公共块面积至少含有三个不同的素因子。该证明结合了从正方形各行上的矩恒等式得到的同余式，以及完美划分的各块具有两两不同高度这一观察；二者共同迫使 $q$ 整除每个块的两条边长，此后可以将坐标同时除以 $q$，使面积中 $q$ 的指数减少 2。本文的所有结果均已在 Lean 4 中形式化并得到验证。
zh.introduction:
蒙德里安艺术问题关注将一个 $n \times n$ 正方形划分为边长为正整数的轴对齐矩形。为了排除如相同平行条带之类的平凡构型，容许划分中的矩形被要求两两不全等：任意两个矩形不能具有相同的无序边长对。划分 $P$ 的缺陷为
$$\text{def}(P) = \max_{R \in P} |R| - \min_{R \in P} |R|,$$
而蒙德里安数 $M(n)$ 则是将 $n \times n$ 正方形划分为两个或更多矩形的所有容许划分中的最小缺陷。

缺陷为零的划分称为完美划分：其矩形两两不全等，但面积均为相同的 $A$，因此当有 $k$ 个矩形时有 $kA = n^2$。正如 arXiv:2610.19193 在第 1 节中所回顾的，是否存在某个 $n$ 使得 $M(n) = 0$ 仍是一个未决问题，尽管人们猜想不存在这样的 $n$。该论文还指出，只要存在一个完美划分就会产生无穷多个，因为将所有边长缩放一个公共因子仍保持缺陷为零，并且通过计算已对所有 $n \le 1000$ 排除了完美划分（arXiv:2311.02385）。在理论方面，素数幂的情形是经典的：边长为素数幂的正方形不存在完美划分（arXiv:2007.09639，Theorem 4.1，通过对可用形状计数），并且密度结果表明有正比例的整数 $n$ 满足 $M(n) > 0$。

本文给出了一个同时适用于所有正方形的阻碍，并且它是用公共块面积而非边长来表述的。主定理 `mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_area` 指出，对于不同素数 $p$ 和 $q$ 以及任意指数 $s$ 和 $t$，任何整数正方形的完美容许划分中，所有块的面积均不可能全为 $q^s p^t$。它推广了针对素数幂面积 $p^t$ 的相同命题 `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area`。这里形式化了两个推论：

- `mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_powers`：对于不同素数 $p, q$ 和所有指数 $e, f$，边长为 $q^f p^e$ 的正方形不存在完美划分。结合素数幂的情形，这排除了至多含有两个不同素因子的所有边长，且对指数没有任何限制。
- `mondrian_perfect_area_three_prime_factors`：在任何正方形的任何完美划分中，公共块面积至少含有三个不同的素因子。

在同一形式化开发中，一个较早且较弱的结果 `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_mul_prime_pow` 通过另一条途径处理了边长 $q p^e$，即计算能放入该正方形内的面积因子对；它是第一推论中 $f = 1$ 的情形。关键的新要素是一个整除性引理：若公共面积为 $q^s p^t$ 且 $q$ 整除 $n$，则 $q$ 整除每个块的两条边长。其证明仅使用了正方形各行上的一个线性恒等式、完美划分中块高度的两两不同性，以及不能被 $q$ 整除的块高度在整除关系下构成一条链这一事实。
zh.preliminaries:
我们遵循 Lean 形式化的约定。

定义 1（`mondrian_rect_width`、`mondrian_rect_height`、`mondrian_rect_area`）。矩形是自然数的四元组 $r = (x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1)$，其左下角为 $(x_0, y_0)$，右上角为 $(x_1, y_1)$。其宽度为 $x_1 - x_0$，高度为 $y_1 - y_0$，其面积为二者的乘积。

定义 2（`mondrian_is_partition`）。对于自然数 $n$ 和矩形列表 $P$，当满足以下条件时 `mondrian_is_partition n P` 成立：
1. $P$ 至少有两个元素；
2. 每个 $r \in P$ 均满足 $x_0 < x_1$ 以及 $y_0 < y_1$；
3. $P$ 的不同项具有不相交的单位元胞集且不全等，其中若两个矩形具有相同的宽度和高度，或者各自的宽度等于另一者的高度，则称这两个矩形全等；
4. 这些矩形的单位元胞的并集恰好是 $\{0, \dots, n-1\} \times \{0, \dots, n-1\}$。

单位元胞以其左下角命名，因此条件 4 说明这些块覆盖了画布 $[0,n] \times [0,n]$ 且没有块超出画布。

定义 3（`mondrian_defect`）。$P$ 的缺陷是各块面积的最大值减去其最小值（空列表取值为 0）。若一个划分的缺陷为 0，则称其为完美划分。

贯穿全文使用了两个基本事实。根据 `mondrian_defect_zero_equal`，缺陷为零的列表中所有块均具有相同的面积。根据 `mondrian_perfect_area_product`，若 $P$ 是 $n$-正方形的一个完美容许划分且 $r \in P$，则 $|P| \cdot \text{area}(r) = n^2$，因为各个块在元胞上是不相交的且覆盖了画布的 $n^2$ 个元胞。
zh.result:
定理（`mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_area`）。设 $p$ 与 $q$ 为不同素数，并设 $s, t, n \in \mathbb{N}$。不存在矩形列表 $P$ 满足 `mondrian_is_partition n P`、`mondrian_defect P = 0` 且每个 $r \in P$ 的面积均为 $q^s p^t$。

该命题对 $n$ 没有施加任何条件：它纯粹是对公共块面积的阻碍。$s = 0$ 的情形是 `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area`，它排除了素数幂公共面积 $p^t$（包括面积 1）。

推论 1（`mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_powers`）。设 $p$ 和 $q$ 为不同素数，且 $e, f \in \mathbb{N}$。则 $\neg \exists P,\ \text{mondrian\_is\_partition}(q^f p^e, P) \wedge \text{mondrian\_defect}(P) = 0$。

事实上，由 `mondrian_perfect_area_product`，完美划分的公共面积整除 $n^2 = q^{2f} p^{2e}$，因此具有 $q^s p^t$ 的形式。每个至多含有两个不同素因子的整数 $n \ge 2$ 都具有 $q^f p^e$ 的形式，所以这样的正方形均不存在完美划分。

推论 2（`mondrian_perfect_area_three_prime_factors`）。若 `mondrian_is_partition n P`、`mondrian_defect P = 0` 且 $r \in P$，则 $r$ 的面积至少有三个不同的素因子。

因此，任何假设存在的完美划分其块面积必须能被三个不同的素数整除，又因为该面积整除 $n^2$，其边长 $n$ 也必须至少含有三个不同的素因子。这些结果留下的最小未决边长为 $30, 42, 60, 66, \dots$；通过 arXiv:2311.02385 的计算，排除了所有不超过 1000 的边长，因此这里的结果补充了双素数边长的无穷族，并对任何反例的面积给出了结构性限制。
zh.proof:
在全文中，$P$ 为 $n \times n$ 正方形的一个完美容许划分；对 $r \in P$，我们用 $w(r)$ 和 $h(r)$ 分别表示其宽度与高度，并用 $r = (x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1)$ 表示其坐标。

步骤 1（不同高度）。$P$ 的两个不同块具有不同的高度。若 $h(r) = h(r')$，由于 $w(r)h(r) = w(r')h(r')$ 且高度为正，则亦有 $w(r) = w(r')$，从而 $r$ 与 $r'$ 全等，但这是容许性所禁止的。

步骤 2（行上的矩恒等式）。对于行水平 $0, 1, \dots, n$ 上的任意整数值函数 $f$，
$$\sum_{r \in P} w(r)\,\bigl(f(y_1(r)) - f(y_0(r))\bigr) = n\,\bigl(f(n) - f(0)\bigr).$$
将 $f(y_1) - f(y_0)$ 写为行 $y_0 \le y < y_1$ 上的裂项和，左侧变为 $\sum_{y < n} (f(y+1) - f(y)) \sum_{r \ni y} w(r)$，而穿过任意行 $y$ 的块宽度之和为 $n$，因为这些块构成了该行元胞的一个划分。

步骤 3（孤立块）。设 $d \mid n$ 且 $m \ge 1$。假设 $r \in P$ 满足 $m \nmid h(r)$，且其他任意块 $r'$ 均满足 $d \mid w(r')$ 或 $m \mid h(r')$。则 $d \mid w(r)$。为此，将步骤 2 应用于如下函数：若 $y \equiv y_1(r) \pmod m$ 则 $f(y) = 1$，否则 $f(y) = 0$。右侧是 $n$ 的倍数，因而也是 $d$ 的倍数。满足 $m \mid h(r')$ 的块 $r'$ 满足 $y_0(r') \equiv y_1(r') \pmod m$，因此其对 $f$ 的增量为 0；满足 $d \mid w(r')$ 的块贡献了 $d$ 的倍数。对于 $r$ 本身，因 $m \nmid h(r)$，有 $y_0(r) \not\equiv y_1(r) \pmod m$，所以其增量恰好为 1，对应的项为 $w(r)$。将该恒等式模 $d$ 化简即得 $d \mid w(r)$。

步骤 4（素数链）。设 $d \mid n$，设 $p$ 为素数且 $C > 0$，并假设宽度不能被 $d$ 整除的每个块其高度均形如 $C p^a$。则每个宽度均能被 $d$ 整除。否则，在满足 $d \nmid w$ 的块中，选取高度 $C p^a$ 最小的块 $z$ 并令 $m = C p^{a+1}$。由于 $0 < h(z) < m$，有 $m \nmid h(z)$。由步骤 1，其他任意满足 $d \nmid w(r')$ 的块 $r'$ 的高度 $C p^b$ 均满足 $C p^b \ne C p^a$，且由极小性有 $C p^b \ge C p^a$，因此 $b \ge a + 1$ 且 $m \mid h(r')$。此时步骤 3 给出 $d \mid w(z)$，矛盾。

步骤 5（两条边均能被 $q$ 整除）。假设每个块的面积均为 $q^s p^t$ 且 $q \mid n$。若 $q \nmid w(r)$，则由 $w(r)h(r) = q^s p^t$ 可知整幂 $q^s$ 整除 $h(r)$，剩余因子为 $p^t$ 的约数，因此存在某个 $a$ 使得 $h(r) = q^s p^a$。取 $d = q$ 及 $C = q^s$ 应用步骤 4 表明 $q$ 整除每个宽度。将相同的论据应用于沿对角线翻转后的划分（该划分同样是完美且容许的），表明 $q$ 整除每个高度。

步骤 6（递降）。若 $q$ 整除 $n$ 且整除每个块的两条边，并且公共面积为 $q^2 B$，则将所有坐标除以 $q$ 即可得到 $(n/q)$-正方形的一个公共面积为 $B$ 的完美容许划分。不相交性、覆盖性以及不全等性均可传递，因为划分后矩形的一个元胞 $(i, j)$ 对应于原矩形的元胞 $(q(i+1) - 1, q(j+1) - 1)$。相同的坐标除法构成了 `mondrian_perfect_partition_div` 的基础。

定理的证明。我们对 $s$ 进行强归纳，同时处理所有的 $n$ 和 $P$。若 $s = 0$，面积为 $p^t$，应用 `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area`。该结果通过单素数 $p$ 的相同方案证明：步骤 5 应用于面积 $p^t$（指数为零的第二个素数）迫使 $p$ 整除每个块的两条边，递降使指数减少 2，而面积 1 是不可能的，因为两个 $1 \times 1$ 的块全等。若 $s \ge 1$，任取 $z \in P$。根据 `mondrian_perfect_area_product`，有 $|P| \cdot q^s p^t = n^2$，故 $q \mid n^2$，从而 $q \mid n$。由步骤 5，$q$ 整除 $z$ 的两条边，所以 $q^2 \mid q^s p^t$；因 $q^2$ 与 $p^t$ 互素，这给出 $s \ge 2$。写作 $q^s p^t = q^2 \cdot q^{s-2} p^t$，步骤 6 给出 $(n/q)$-正方形的一个公共面积为 $q^{s-2} p^t$ 的完美容许划分，而这由针对 $s - 2 < s$ 的归纳假设所排除。

推论 1 的证明。$f = 0$ 的情形即为素数幂边长情形 `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power`。对于 $f \ge 1$，根据 `mondrian_perfect_area_product`，公共面积 $A$ 整除 $q^{2f} p^{2e}$，因此 $A = q^s p^t$，且相同的整除性与递降步骤将边长从 $q^{f} p^e$ 降为 $q^{f-1} p^e$，从而完成了对 $f$ 的归纳。

推论 2 的证明。假设公共面积 $A$ 至多含有两个不同的素因子。由于它是正数，因此它只能是 1、素数幂 $p^t$，或满足 $p \ne q$ 的 $q^s p^t$。面积 1 是不可能的，因为所有块都将是全等的单位正方形；另外两种情形分别由 `mondrian_no_perfect_prime_power_area` 和 `mondrian_no_perfect_two_prime_area` 所排除。
zh.discussion:
该定理表明，无论正方形的大小为何，完美蒙德里安划分的公共块面积均不可能仅由两个素数支撑。其推论排除了至多含有两个不同素因子的所有边长，并表明零缺陷猜想的反例需要其块面积（从而边长）至少能被三个不同的素数整除。

该论证基于正方形各行上的一个线性恒等式以及块高度的两两互异性。步骤 3 利用行的剩余类的指示函数孤立出一个块；只要与 $d$ 互素的宽度的块高度构成一条链 $C p^a$，步骤 4 就能实现这一点，因为此时其中最小者是唯一一个高度不能被链中下一个元素整除的块。在两个素数的情形下，与 $q$ 互素的宽度的余因子被迫处于这样的一条链中。当面积中出现第三个素数 $\ell$ 时，与 $q$ 互素的宽度留下的高度为 $q^s p^a \ell^b$，而这些数在整除关系下不再构成全序，因此孤立步骤无法直接应用。

arXiv:2610.19193 第 1 节中回顾的核心问题——是否存在某个 $n \ge 3$ 使得 $M(n) = 0$——仍然悬而未决。这些结果未涵盖的最小边长（例如 $30 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$）仅被 arXiv:2311.02385 中针对 $n \le 1000$ 的计算所排除，并且对于具有三个或更多不同素因子的边长，目前尚无统一的论证方法。
